title: Interleave Halves of Linked List
description:
Given the `head` of a singly linked list of length `n`, split the list into a first half of length `ceil(n / 2)` (`a_0, a_1, ..., a_{p-1}`) and a second half of length `floor(n / 2)` (`b_0, b_1, ..., b_{q-1}`), preserving the original order within each half.

Interleave the two halves alternately as `a_0 -> b_0 -> a_1 -> b_1 -> ...` (if `n` is odd, `a_{p-1}` appears at the end), and return the head of the modified list. Solve it in-place in `O(1)` extra space.
constraints: The number of nodes in the list is in the range [0, 5000].
hints: Initialize `slow = head` and `fast = head.next`; advancing `slow` by 1 and `fast` by 2 stops `slow` at the tail of the first half (length `ceil(n / 2)`).
Detach the second half at `second = slow.next; slow.next = null`, then weave nodes from `first` and `second` in alternating order without reversing either half.

examples.explanation: A 2-node list has halves [10] and [20], which stays [10, 20].
